patient.chief_complaint: Sudden onset worst headache of life while lifting at work, vomiting, brought by ambulance
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Brooks is a 51-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension who was brought by ambulance from his workplace after sudden onset severe headache. He was lifting a heavy crate when he developed an instantaneous, explosive headache that he describes as 'like a bomb went off in my head,' immediately rated 10/10. He vomited three times and his coworkers found him holding his head and called 911. EMS reports BP 224/138 mmHg at the scene. He remained conscious throughout. He arrived by ambulance and is in obvious distress from the headache. He reports neck stiffness that began about 30 minutes after the headache onset. He has no prior history of similar headaches. He denies focal weakness or vision changes. He denies loss of consciousness. The presentation is classic for aneurysmal SAH: instantaneous maximal thunderclap headache during Valsalva maneuver (heavy lifting), with vomiting and neck stiffness.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; extreme pain distress; photophobic and phonophobic
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 4mm; EOM intact; no papilledema; no ptosis; no CN III palsy; no facial droop
neurological_exam.motor: 5/5 strength all four extremities; no pronator drift
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric; plantar responses flexor bilaterally
neurological_exam.additional: Marked nuchal rigidity: chin-to-chest restricted by 4 cm; Kernig sign positive; Brudzinski sign positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Extensive thick hyperdense blood filling suprasellar cistern, interpeduncular fossa, and ambient cisterns
Small amount of blood in third ventricle
Mild dilation of lateral ventricles - early communicating hydrocephalus

ct.impression: Extensive subarachnoid hemorrhage (Fisher grade 4) with intraventricular extension and early communicating hydrocephalus. Classic aneurysmal SAH pattern. Immediate CTA for aneurysm identification. Neurosurgery for EVD consideration.
recommended_actions: Neurosurgery consult - consider EVD for hydrocephalus

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 17.2 x10^9/L (H), BUN 22 mg/dL (H), Glucose 228 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.38 ng/mL (H), BNP 342 pg/mL (H).

special_tests.Xanthochromia: Definite - yellow CSF supernatant visible and spectrophotometry confirmed

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 34 cmH2O. WBC: N/A (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 286 mg/dL. Glucose: 114 mg/dL (serum 228, ratio 0.50) (ratio 0.50). Xanthochromia: Definite - yellow CSF supernatant visible and spectrophotometry confirmed.

findings.finding: Large ruptured saccular aneurysm 8.2 x 7.1 mm with broad-based neck 4.6 mm and multilobulated dome

output.impression: Large AComA aneurysm 8.2 mm with wide neck consistent with ruptured aneurysm. Conventional DSA for treatment planning. Wide neck may require balloon-assisted or stent-assisted coiling, or surgical clipping.
recommended_actions: Neurovascular team decision: coiling vs clipping for wide-necked aneurysm

output.wall_motion: Severe apical akinesis, basal hyperkinesis - classic Takotsubo
output.impression: Severe neurogenic Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. EF severely reduced 38%. High risk of cardiogenic shock with aggressive triple-H therapy.
recommended_actions: Avoid aggressive triple-H given low EF

findings.status: Severe bilateral ACA vasospasm - AComA territory

quantitative_data.clinical: New bifrontal confusion and leg weakness

output.impression: Severe bilateral ACA/MCA vasospasm on day 8 with new neurological deficits. DCI established. CT perfusion urgent. Intra-arterial therapy likely needed.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: Serum sodium Day 4 126 mEq/L (L), Urine sodium Day 4 88 mEq/L (H).

warnings: Hold lisinopril and HCTZ during acute SAH phase
Target SBP 140-160 before aneurysm secured; 120-140 after

findings.location: Bilateral frontal lobes and anterior MCA territories
findings.description: Severely reduced CBF 18-24 mL/100g/min - below infarction threshold
Early established infarction on diffusion trace

output.impression: Critical bilateral anterior circulation perfusion compromise with evolving infarction right frontal. DCI established. Emergency intra-arterial intervention required immediately.
recommended_actions: Emergency DSA for intra-arterial therapy NOW

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from large AComA aneurysm with severe DCI (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 4)

differential.key_features: Subarachnoid (not parenchymal) distribution on CT; aneurysm on CTA
CT shows extensive blood; CTA shows aneurysm; CSF bloody
CSF bloody not purulent; glucose ratio normal; no fever; no neutrophilic pleocytosis

optimal_actions.action: CT head - extensive Fisher 4 SAH with IVH and hydrocephalus
Interpret labs - stress leukocytosis, troponin, glucose (diabetes)

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Deep T inversions, QTc 512 ms - critical arrhythmia risk
Hold HCTZ and lisinopril - additive hypotension with nimodipine
Day 4 Na 126 with high urine Na - CSW, treat with hypertonic saline not fluid restriction

critical_actions: CTA urgently for AComA aneurysm identification
Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days - start immediately
Hold lisinopril and HCTZ - additive hypotension with nimodipine
QTc 512 ms - avoid all QT-prolonging drugs
Monitor sodium daily - severe CSW requires hypertonic saline (NOT fluid restriction)
EVD consideration for hydrocephalus and IVH
contraindicated_actions: Do not restrict fluids for hyponatremia in SAH without distinguishing CSW from SIADH
Do not continue antihypertensives with nimodipine
Do not give QT-prolonging antiemetics given QTc 512 ms
key_reasoning_points: Classic presentation: instantaneous maximal headache + Valsalva trigger + vomiting + meningism = textbook SAH
Fisher grade 4 SAH predicts very high vasospasm risk - DCI develops on day 8 requiring emergency intervention
Cerebral salt wasting (Na 126, high urine Na) vs SIADH distinction is critical: CSW requires IV saline, SIADH requires fluid restriction
Large AComA aneurysm (8.2 mm) with wide neck requires discussion of coiling vs clipping approach
Severe Takotsubo (EF 38%) limits aggressive triple-H therapy options during vasospasm
QTc 512 ms with neurogenic changes: absolute contraindication to QT-prolonging drugs
